reviews.title: A chat system built in the 90's
reviews.text: This app is ridiculously underwhelming.  They charge a premium price (too much) for their services and give you an app that runs like it was built in 1995.   The app isn't scaled to the full screen, but instead you see it as though it's scaled for your iPhone in a partial screen.  The only way to really use the service comfortably is to log in on a web browser.   The actual chat part of it is completely outdated too.  Minimal options, no attachment functions, no editing, seriously poor design.  Facebook dating is years ahead in design and it's free.  Come on Match - when's the last time you actually updated functionality instead of  just throwing bandaids on app issues.  Horrible design overall, overpriced, and limited membership now-a-days.

reviews.title: ⭐ 1/5 — A Dating App Disguised as a Paywall
reviews.text:
Absolutely horrible experience! Match has mastered one thing: charging you for practically everything. People can like your profile and even send you messages, but you can’t see who they are or read those messages without being pushed to subscribe.

And apparently, paying isn’t enough unless you choose the right subscription tier! Different features come with different price tags.

What’s the point of a dating app that tells you someone is interested but puts a price tag on finding out who?

At this point, it feels less like a dating platform and more like a money grab.

If connecting people were really the priority, basic communication wouldn’t be treated like a luxury upgrade.

reviews.title: Ban you without cause
reviews.text: I was on OK Cupid and an offer appeared to try Match, so I thought “why not?” I downloaded the app, logged in, and created a basic profile with a picture and using the same bio as on OK Cupid. Scrolled through a couple profiles, didn’t do anything else, put my phone down and got sidetracked with something. I came back ~20 mins later and found myself banned. No explanation. I reached out to support asking what I did wrong. They replied that I had violated the terms of service, that I was banned, and that the decision was final. No explanation of what I supposedly did. My OK Cupid profile was still totally fine. And considering all I had done to that point was create my basic profile on Match…all I can say is that I’m pretty sure this was discrimination on some level. I read through the entire terms of service to try to figure out what I might have violated, and found nothing. Someone at Match probably felt I wasn’t a good fit for the platform or something and banned me. Considering OK Cupid is also owned by MatchGrouo, I stopped using it.   I won’t be using any app owned by MatchGroup ever again.

reviews.title: Atrocious
reviews.text: Today marks my 7th day of investment and 11th email exchange to gain a refund. The refund was not initially requested due to dissatisfaction of service but due to  my concern of data breach and highly unusual activity on the platform as to which I am sure many have testified prior to me. Fake accounts. Suspicious rhythms of communication that often lead to a request for personal information within the first three messages. A lack of verified profiles with little to not information. It is my assumption that photos might be being utilized of former account holders, or unaware owners of photos, at least. After a week of correspondence I have been told that I cannot be refunded as they have no way to refund me as my account is now deleted, yet they still have access to my bank account to charge me four days past I was told in bold letters that “you will not be charged again,” on the 26th of May with my bank having a pending charge on the 29th. Do better Match. You are in the hospitality business. These simple exchanges should be exactly that, simple. My advice. Stay away from Match. I am assuming that these platforms are being overrun either voluntarily or without strategy of recourse to deal with AI and phishing. All said, such a disappointing experience completely unrelated to what should be the focus of the service offering. Basic business.

I have had 5 conversations (out of hundreds of likes sent, maybe 20 received, maybe 5 were real).  In every conversation they just stopped communicating in the middle of the chat. Ghost.  I have not even met someone for coffee.  I think Match pays women to make fake accounts.  And the few women that are actually on, just all want the tall good looking guy with money.  And they will ghost you as soon as someone they think is better messages. Perfect combination of capitalistic greed and the chaos of social interaction. Save your money men, THEY ARE ALL FAKE.
